answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a island as the anchor of the cost. A jetty stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a marble holds the rep...
